rows.why: What each tool and MCP server connects to and can reach (backends, data stores, external networks) is documented, so the AI's real reach through its tools is known.
The tool actions that need a human to confirm before the AI runs them (writes, payments, deletions, outbound sends) are identified and that confirmation step is in place.
The MCP servers and tools the AI can call, hosted inside or used from outside, are identified with their source, version, owner or provider and declared capabilities.
Each tool or outside MCP server is reviewed before use for the systems and data it can touch, its declared capabilities and scopes, and who runs it, with controls set to match.
The harm a misused tool could do (acting with borrowed user permissions, confused-deputy calls, tool poisoning) is threat-modelled for likelihood and impact, and redone when tools change.
Tool use in production is monitored and reviewed for anomalies, unauthorised calls and use beyond the approved capabilities.
Tools and MCP servers are security tested, including authorization enforcement and adversarial prompts that try to make the AI misuse a tool, and the results are documented.
Tool calls are logged with the user and client identity, credentials, tool and parameters used and the result, including logs from outside servers, so every action can be traced.

Each tool and server gets access through an approved grant with its own least-privilege credentials and scopes, reviewed against actual use and separated from production and other servers, rather than human-sized or borrowed user permissions.
When a new risk surfaces for a tool (an unapproved server, a new capability on a known server, a disclosed vulnerability) it is triaged, contained and fixed before use continues.
A tool or MCP server can be switched off quickly, with its tokens revoked and sessions ended, and someone is named to do it.
Outside MCP servers and their providers are held to security terms and regularly monitored for capability, authorization and version changes and for support status.
Incidents involving tools (unauthorised invocations, compromised servers, stolen tokens) are reported, handled with outside server operators where needed, reviewed afterwards and recorded.
